summary: This article surveys ghost stories and hauntings across cultures in autumn 2023, arguing that they let people confront death, memory, and the unknown. It presents voices from Puerto Rico, Scotland, the American South and Texas, Japan, Salem, and online communities, plus scholarly commentary from an anthropologist and a philosopher. It concludes that ghost stories invite reflection on the human condition, even as digital platforms become the new place for sharing them.
one_line: A 2023 survey of regional hauntings and ghost lore worldwide, showing how ghost stories help cultures confront death, memory, and existential questions.
key_facts: The article marks the autumn equinox of September 21, 2023 as the start of a season suited to ghost stories.
Dr. Eliza Montgomery, an anthropologist from the University of Lore and Legends, began her study on October 13, 2023 and says hauntings reflect 'the collective conscience'.

On October 17, 2023, tour guide Maria Alvarez led a group through Old San Juan, Puerto Rico, recounting tales of colonial spirits; she calls them 'a collective memory of the past that refuses to be forgotten'.
Edinburgh storyteller Douglas McEwan told a tale on October 31, 2023 about the restless specter of a laird wrongfully betrayed generations ago, heard when the veil between worlds is thinnest.
Louisiana historian Jasmine Carter narrated the history of the Myrtles Plantation on November 2, 2023, saying 'each ghost carries a story'.
Paranormal investigator Eli Sutton documented spectral occurrences at an abandoned homestead outside Amarillo, Texas on September 28, 2023.
Yuki Ono, a Shinto practitioner in Japan, said on October 10, 2023 that kami are guardians and 'a link to the divine' rather than spirits meant to instill fear.
Cyberpsychologist Ava Chen released a paper on November 10, 2023 arguing digital platforms are 'the new campfires' for ghost tales and form a 'shared digital folklore'.

Salem, Massachusetts has gained tourism from its witch trial history; Heather O'Riley of the planning committee for the Salem Witch Festival (October 31, 2023) calls it 'a touchstone for exploring the darker corners of history and the human psyche'.
Professor Jacob Wei of the University of Thought, in a lecture on metaphysics and mortality on October 3, 2023, called the apparition 'an encounter with the unresolved'.
The article concludes that ghost stories invite people to face fear, nostalgia, and the tension between longing for immortality and accepting a fleeting nature.
